comment: The generic Uncharted patch (issues #221 and #222, of #206): the one finished embroidered patch that stands for every bird outside every set, in place of the empty canvas round, with the bird's name on its paper tag. `shipped` is the maintainer's pick of the lettered `candidates` (A, the feather, on 2026-11-26, recorded on #221): the cut painting and the painting as it came, both in `art/uncharted/`, and the two files the app lights it from, which `scripts/uncharted-candidates.py layers` made from the cut as a pack's patch is made (`ground` and `stitch_bounds` are that patch row's, and `PatchArt.uncharted`'s). `packbuilder/tests/test_uncharted_patch.py` holds the files to these hashes. The rest is how it was painted, and what else was tried. Painted by FLUX.3 Image Klein from text alone (the `workflow`, on the square `canvas` the mascot patches use), in the language of the real patches (`patch-prompts.json`): a merit badge lying flat on white card under even light, so the app does the lighting. The badge is Uncharted's own (`PatchEdition.of(setID: nil)`): the plain canvas round with the brown cord, so it still reads as outside every set, and the thread is that brown and cream, so no emblem claims a plumage. `emblems` are what was tried, each no particular species: the ticket's feather, plain bird and compass, and three more. `placement` (an emblem may have its own) keeps the embroidery in the bottom third: the bird's name hangs on a paper tag from a slot a tenth of the way down (`TiedTag`), and a three-line name on a board's tile reaches 0.56 of the way down. The wording was found by trial: 'within its lower half' and 'about a third as tall' put the emblem under the tag, 'a narrow band of bare canvas between it and the lower border' stitched a seam across the badge, and a strap made the binoculars a smiling face. FLUX.3 reads a caption of the finished picture. `candidates` pins what went on the maintainer's sheet, lettered as there: the emblem, its seed and the cut patch's SHA-256; the same prompt and seed paint the same picture again. Bump the version when the template, the placement or an emblem changes.
template: A product photograph of an embroidered merit badge shaped like a perfect circle, photographed from directly above, lying flat in the middle of plain white card under soft, even, diffuse light, with only a faint shadow. The badge is plain natural undyed cotton canvas, an oatmeal-beige cloth with a visible plain weave, the same colour everywhere inside the border, finished with a wide, thick, raised merrowed border of overlocked dark umber-brown thread, the deep brown of coffee, all the way around its edge. {emblem} {placement} Nothing else is stitched on the badge: the rest of it is bare canvas. Every thread is visible: the soft sheen of rayon, the raised stitches, the plain weave of the canvas between them. The whole badge is in the frame with a margin of white card all around it, in sharp focus. No text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere. No people.
placement: The embroidery is small, about a quarter as tall as the badge, and sits at the bottom of the badge, centred left to right, close to the lower border without touching it: all of it is in the bottom third of the badge. The upper two thirds of the badge are empty bare canvas, with no line or seam across it.

feather.title: A feather
feather.emblem: Embroidered on it is a single plain bird's feather lying on its side, almost level, its quill at the left and its soft rounded tip at the right, with a gentle curve along its length. Its vane is laid in slanting satin stitches in warm cream, fawn and umber-brown thread, darker towards the tip, split by a few natural gaps in the barbs, and its shaft is one fine line of pale thread. It is no particular bird's feather: no eye-spot, no bars, no bright colour.
feather.placement: The embroidery is small and sits at the very bottom of the badge, just above the lower border: all of it is in the bottom third of the badge, centred left to right. The upper two thirds of the badge are empty bare canvas.

bird.title: A plain bird
bird.emblem: Embroidered on it is one small plain songbird in side view, a simple stylised silhouette like a folk-art bird: a round head, a short pointed bill, a plump body, a folded wing and a short tail, standing on a short bare twig. Its whole body is filled with satin stitch in a single umber-brown thread, the same brown as the border, with only the edge of its wing picked out in one line of cream thread and a tiny cream dot for its eye. It has no markings, no streaks, no crest and no bright colour: it is no particular kind of bird.

compass.title: A compass rose
compass.emblem: Embroidered on it is a compass rose, as on an old map: an eight-pointed star with four long slender points to the top, bottom, left and right and four shorter points between them, each point split down its middle into a umber-brown half and a cream half in satin stitch, inside a thin ring of stitched brown thread with a few short tick marks. There are no letters on it.

flight.title: A bird in flight on a dashed trail
flight.emblem: Embroidered on it is one small plain bird in flight seen from the side, a simple stylised silhouette with its two wings raised in a shallow V, filled with satin stitch in a single umber-brown thread with no markings, and behind it a curving trail of short dashes in cream running stitch, like a route drawn on a map, looping once before it reaches the bird. It is no particular kind of bird.

binoculars.title: Binoculars
binoculars.emblem: Embroidered on it is a small pair of birdwatcher's binoculars seen from the front and a little above, a simple stylised shape: two short barrels side by side joined by a bridge, in satin stitch in umber-brown thread with cream bands and two round lenses of muted teal thread. They have no strap and no cord: nothing hangs from them.

nest.title: A nest with eggs
nest.emblem: Embroidered on it is a small bird's nest seen from the side and a little above, a shallow cup woven of fawn and umber-brown straight stitches crossing like twigs and dry grass, holding three plain cream eggs in satin stitch. The eggs have no speckles and no colour: they are no particular bird's.
